focus: What the word 'goal' naming four unrelated things actually costs; rename, note or nothing; every file a rename would touch
novelty: Separated the one collision with live machinery from three harmless name overlaps, and priced the rename at thirteen live files by splitting live citations from historical records.

label: Only one of the four referents is a real collision; the session goal and the packet goal are one system by design
detail: (1) packet goal.md 194 files; (2) session goal = its runtime projection; (3) deep-review goal-file-manifest.txt with two parsers and a test; (4) ClickUp goals card self-declared UNSUPPORTED. Renaming the session vocabulary would undo the unification; the ClickUp card is namespaced.
novelty: counts machinery per referent instead of treating four names as four problems

label: The disambiguation already exists, in the document whose readers need it least
detail: The engine README warns that goal-file-manifest.txt and ClickUp goals share the word. The reader at risk is reading deep-review assets or a packet manifest, where no warning exists. The note's placement is the defect.
novelty: the cost is already being paid, in the wrong place

label: The manifest name reaches a workflow, a gate and a live test, none of which is about a packet goal
detail: Three consumers treat it as review scope: the resolve step declares scope from it, the checker asserts trackedness, the vitest spawns the checker three times. The name says goal; every consumer means review scope.
novelty: the machinery census for the collision

label: The rename touches thirteen live files; ~60 historical citations must not be rewritten
sources: rg -l over specs/.opencode/.github excluding lineages, containment, .worktrees
per-file reads of every live citation
detail: Six manifest files; deep-review-auto.yaml:373-374; the checker script (name, line 5 default, line 21 temp prefix); the vitest path constant; the engine README note line 21; three packet docs (005-blocker-closeout spec/plan/tasks). Review iteration records, prompt archives and deltas stay as evidence of past runs.

label: No in-repo consumer reads the manifest outside the enumerated files; out-of-repo consumers are INFERRED absent
detail: INFERRED: an external consumer could read a manifest by name. Settling action: operator check of downstream automation; no evidence of one exists.
novelty: bounded uncertainty instead of an unqualified claim
